newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania urges deadline for power deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania urges deadline for power deregulation.

text.p: Pennsylvania's congressional delegation urged the House Commerce Committee to pass a bill to set a deadline for all U.S. states to open local power markets to competition, according to a letter released Wednesday.
Pennsylvania itself is phasing in electricity competition from 1999 and wants utilities in its state to have access to markets in other states.

"A federal date for state implementation, coupled with interim reciprocity protection, will help to assure fairness," all 23 members of Pennsylvania's House and Senate delegation said in a June 26 letter to Commerce Committee leaders.
Commerce Committee Chairman Thomas Bliley, a Virginia Republican, pointed to the letter as an example of growing support for power market deregulation.

"Democrats and Republicans alike in both the House and Senate ... have stood as one. Uniformly they have said that a federal date certain for nationwide competition is the best way to ensure fairness," Bliley said in a statement.
"Needless to say, that's an approach I agree with," he added. Bliley has said he wants to pass a bill in this congress to make states deregulate local power markets.
